Subject: Quick clarifications on what Redwood keeps by default

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking a look at our security questionnaire last week. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering and legal teams about default capture behavior so we can complete our intake:

- What does Redwood retain by default for a hosted API request? Specifically: original prompt (user input), streamed token fragments, final generated output, and any KV cache or session-affinity artifacts?
- Are streamed tokens treated as persisted logs or ephemeral buffers? If persisted, what is the retention window and where do they live (region)?
- If we upload attachments (e.g., a PDF during a request), are those stored with the request and for how long?
- If we ask Redwood to perform an erase (API/portal), what evidence do you provide and how long until the artifacts are actually removed from all storage tiers?

We need clear answers we can pass to our compliance team (ideally with exact retention windows and the erasure timeline).

Thanks,

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary of default behavior for hosted API customers (we can produce a formal PDF for procurement/legal if that helps). I've kept the language concrete so it's straightforward for your intake checklist.

Summary (defaults, hosted API):
- Original prompts / requests (full user input): retained by default for 30 days for operational troubleshooting and billing reconciliation. These are stored in the region you select at account creation (US/EU/APAC) unless you choose a residency override.
- Streamed token fragments (intermediate streaming buffers): treated as ephemeral buffers for real-time reconstruction. By default they are kept only long enough to assemble the stream and are tombstoned within 1 hour. They are not indexed for search or model training.
- Final generated outputs (completions): retained by default for 90 days for quality-monitoring and metric aggregation. Note: outputs are used for aggregated quality analytics only and are not used to fine-tune models without explicit opt-in.
- KV cache / session-affinity artifacts: these are per-session ephemeral caches that are flushed on session termination; default retention is session lifetime + 2 hours to allow safe autoscaling, after which they are purged.
- Attachments uploaded with a request: stored as request-level artifacts and inherit the request retention window (30 days) unless you configure a longer storage class.

Erase requests and evidence:
- Customers can request erasure via the API or the Console. We initiate physical deletion within 24 hours of a validated erase request. Depending on underlying storage tiers and backup maintenance windows, final expungement across all replicated systems can take up to 72 hours (we provide a deletion job id and timestamp).
- Evidence: we return a deletion receipt (job id) and a signed log entry you can use for audit. For enterprise/legal holds we can provide a dated export showing the deletion request and the storage shards affected.

Residency notes:
- Retention windows above are per-region by default. If you select EU residency, both request and artifact copies are kept only in EU regions and subject to the same time horizons.

I'll loop in Kimberly on the evidence and SLA bits (she handles erasure proofing). If you'd like, we can produce a short PDF summary + a checklist specific to BrightBank's evidence requirements.

Thanks Marissa — a couple of operational clarifications from my side:

- Backups and retention windows: backups are on a different cadence. While the user-visible retention windows above are what governs indexable copies and artifacts, backups are rotated and retained according to our backup policy (generally 30 days for hot backups, snapshots may be retained longer for disaster recovery). We do not read or use backup data for analytics.
- Erasure propagation: after we mark data for deletion we purge active replicas first; snapshot removal is queued and controlled by our infra retention process. In the deletion receipt we supply the list of active replica ids and the snapshot ids queued for truncation —this is what customers use as erasure evidence.
- Streaming disclaimers: streamed token fragments are only logged when a customer explicitly enables streaming-recording for debugging; otherwise fragments are transient. If BrightBank wants to record streams for troubleshooting, we recommend a short TTL (1–7 days) and to enable EU residency if you need EU-only storage.

If BrightBank's DPO needs a formal statement (signed) that includes the deletion receipt format and example job ids, we can attach that to the procurement packet.

Kimberly Park

Attachments included:

- requested-evidence-matrix.xlsx — example deletion receipt formats, sample job ids, and the list of replica/snapshot ids we provide for an erase event.

A couple of extra bullets that may help your intake checklist:
- Opt-out: Hosted API customers can set account flags to disable retention of prompts or outputs entirely; doing so will limit some debugging capabilities and may affect billing reconciliation.
- Billing records: we retain minimal billing metadata (transaction id, token counts) for 365 days to support invoicing; this metadata does not include prompt/response payloads.
- Audit hold: if BrightBank requests an audit hold prior to erasure, we will preserve the artifacts and mark them with a legal-hold tag and provide a timeline for release.
